title: Sentence Similarity III
summary: Given two sentences, each made of words separated by spaces, determine if one can be made identical to the other by inserting an arbitrary sentence (possibly empty) within one of them.
statement: Given two sentences, each made of words separated by spaces, determine if one can be made identical to the other by inserting an arbitrary sentence (possibly empty) within one of them. The inserted sentence must be separated by spaces. For example, 'Hello Jane' and 'Hello my name is Jane' are similar because 'my name is' can be inserted between 'Hello' and 'Jane'. However, 'Frog cool' and 'Frogs are cool' are not similar because inserting 's are' does not maintain the required spacing.
constraints: Words are separated by single spaces without leading or trailing spaces.
Return whether inserting one contiguous sequence of whole words into either sentence can make them equal.
reference_solution:
def are_sentences_similar(sentence1, sentence2):
 first,second=sentence1.split(),sentence2.split()
 if len(first)>len(second):first,second=second,first
 prefix=0
 while prefix<len(first) and first[prefix]==second[prefix]:prefix+=1
 suffix=0
 while suffix<len(first)-prefix and first[-1-suffix]==second[-1-suffix]:suffix+=1
 return prefix+suffix>=len(first)

hints: The shorter sentence must remain as a prefix plus a suffix of the longer one.
Count matching words from the left and independently from the right.
Similarity holds when those counts cover every word of the shorter sentence.
The uncovered middle of the longer sentence is exactly one insertable block; if any shorter word remains uncovered, no single insertion can preserve order.
